draft.title: Composite areas
card: A composite shape is made of simpler shapes, such as rectangles, triangles, trapeziums and parts of circles. Split it up, find each area, then add them.
If a piece is cut out of a shape, find the area of the whole shape and subtract the area of the piece.
Use \(A = lw\) for a rectangle, \(A = \frac{1}{2}bh\) for a triangle and \(A = \pi r^{2}\) for a circle. A semicircle is half a circle. The radius is half the diameter.
Example: a 10 m by 6 m rectangle has a semicircle of diameter 6 m on one end. Area \(= 60 + \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 3^{2} \approx 74.1 \text{ m}^{2}\).
draft.remember: Add the parts that join on. Subtract the parts that are cut out.

a.q: A rectangle 8 m by 5 m has a triangle cut out of it. The triangle has base 4 m and height 3 m. What is the area left?
a.why: The rectangle is \(8 \times 5 = 40 \text{ m}^{2}\) and the triangle is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3 = 6 \text{ m}^{2}\). The piece is cut out, so \(40 - 6 = 34 \text{ m}^{2}\). Adding gives \(46 \text{ m}^{2}\), which treats the cut-out as extra area.
a.clue: Is the triangle added to the rectangle or taken from it?

b.q: Mia's rectangular lawn in Dubbo is 10 m by 6 m. It has a circular pond of diameter 4 m in it. What is the area of grass, to one decimal place?
b.why: The pond has radius 2 m, so its area is \(\pi \times 2^{2} \approx 12.57 \text{ m}^{2}\). Grass area \(= 60 - 12.57 \approx 47.4 \text{ m}^{2}\). Using 4 m as the radius gives \(9.7 \text{ m}^{2}\), which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: The formula needs the radius, not the diameter.

wants.brief: A rectangle 10 m long and 6 m wide with a semicircle of diameter 6 m joined to one 6 m end. The rectangle, the semicircle and all lengths are labelled.
wants.why: It shows how the shape splits into a rectangle and a semicircle that are added.
